market_holds: Spot about $4.94-5.00 (Yahoo bars; sealed baseline 5.00 at 18:14 UTC), up 17.1% over 20 sessions but drifting down today from a 5.63 high on about 20k shares. No option market; usual move from history: the opening gap after the last seven prints was -4.8, -3.1, +0.2, -3.9, +1.9, +8.7, -7.3% (own arithmetic from Yahoo daily bars), median absolute about 4%, five of seven negative. The last print (Sep 28, Q4 FY26) was a record $8.8M quarter, but the stock opened -7.3% on the FY27 guide: revenue $30-33M, flat with FY26, adj. EBITDA -$1.2M to -$1.7M, attributed entirely to a pause at the satellite customer, with that customer's revenue guided down about 40% sequentially in Q1 and lower again in Q2, recovery by fiscal year-end, quarterly losses in H1. Consensus for Q1 (single analyst, Lucid Capital, Buy, $8 PT since May 2026) is reported as revenue $6.4M and EPS -$0.13 (Benzinga table via search; its age could not be verified). Since then, Nov 5: a $2M follow-on satellite order shipping from December, 'sooner than anticipated'; the stock went 4.84 to 5.23 over the next week, so that news is at least partly in the price.
view: The decisive fact for Q1 is in place. On Sep 28, two days before the quarter closed, management said the 40% cut applies to the satellite customer's revenue, not to total revenue (TradingKey transcript). That customer was running at about $12-13M a year at the end of Q4, roughly $3.1M a quarter. Cutting it 40% removes about $1.25M, which points to a Q1 of roughly $7.0-7.6M if the other lines held at Q4 levels. That is above the $6.4M consensus, and at those revenues my rough P&L puts the loss nearer -$0.09 a share than -$0.13. So a modest beat on the headline bar is more likely than not. Against that: Q4 margin carried about 3 points of one-time IEEPA tariff refunds; the loss will look poor beside Q4's near-breakeven; the other lines are lumpy, and the other 27% customer and engineering revenue could dip; and the Q2 'further reduction' still has to be sized on the call. The bigger swing factor is the call. The Nov 5 order brings the satellite restart forward from 'end of FY27' to December-February, which would let management sound firmer on the guide or narrow it upward. But that order is already public and the stock ran about 8% on it. This is a $5 microcap trading about $100k a day, where the opening print is thin and has gapped down after five of the last seven releases. The net is a slight upward tilt that I cannot turn into a confident call.
unpriced: Possibly the size of Q1 revenue against a single-analyst $6.4M bar that may have read the 40% cut as falling on total revenue (the wire, e.g. Earnings Whispers, wrote '40% revenue reduction in the September quarter'), when the transcript applies it to one customer. This is weak: I could not verify how old the consensus is, and the price may simply not trade on it.

recommendation.reason: The arithmetic from management's own segment guide points to Q1 revenue above the $6.4M consensus. But the bar is one analyst's number of unknown age, the restart news is public and has run the stock about 8% in a week, and the opening print in this thin microcap has gapped down after most releases. The tilt is real but well short of 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q1 revenue below about $6.5M, or the call trimming the FY27 $30-33M range or putting the December-quarter dip deeper than the satellite cut alone implies.

self_critique: My beat case depends on the 'other' lines holding at Q4 levels and on a consensus number whose date I cannot confirm. If the analyst updated to around $7M after the call, there is no surprise at all. The 41%-of-revenue customer may be the satellite customer, so lumpy shipment timing could cut Q1 deeper than a clean 40%. And the stock already ran 17% into a thin print that tends to open lower.
approach_notes: P4 (prove what is priced) and P3 (freshest data first) helped: the transcript pinned down which base the 40% applies to, and that settled the main question. The thin-baseline microcap left no option or positioning data, so P6's positioning step had nothing to work with.
